clue.text: One with a constructive attitude towards work

definitions.text: One with a constructive attitude towards work

blocks.clueFragment: One with a constructive attitude towards work
blocks.note: surface reading: a cooperative, positive employee
setter's reading: someone whose work is literally constructing things, such as houses

explanation.walkthrough: 'Constructive attitude' sounds like praise for a helpful colleague; taken literally it describes a tradesperson who puts up buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who builds houses and walls is literally constructive in their daily trade.

clue.text: Tense in the saddle? Gets drunk!

blocks.note: a rider in the saddle is said to be up
tight is informal for drunk

explanation.surface: A rider tense on horseback who then goes off and gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing, a jockey who is riding is 'up', as in 'with Dettori up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uptight is anxious and nervous, which is what being tense means.

clue.text: Sign that support had left one at the start

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
the Roman numeral for one
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A sign that a bit of support had been abandoned at the very beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the start' tells you the left-and-one pair goes in front of the support.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, the scales.

clue.text: Give the right call

blocks.note: first meaning: to grant someone a claim or permission
second meaning: to give a title or name to something

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'make the correct call'; the split comes after 'right'.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle is both to grant a claim and to give a book or person a title, that is, to name it.

clue.text: Furry coat is interrupting fitful sleep

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece sits inside the other
fitful means disturbed and irregular, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters of sleep rearranged

explanation.surface: A cosy fur coat that keeps waking someone from a restless night's sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: IS goes into the rearranged sleep after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelisse is a long cloak or coat, often fur-lined or fur-trimmed.

clue.text: One who deserves a pay packet

blocks.note: first meaning: a person who merits or wins something by effort
second meaning: a source of income

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one description of a deserving worker; split after 'deserves', the second half is British slang for something that brings in money.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to deserve by effort, and in British slang a lucrative job or scheme is a nice little earner, bringing income.

clue.text: Frequency of occurrence when another nine detectives were in church

indicators.note: another version of the word means a different arrangement of its letters
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: the letters of nine rearranged
the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch
the Church of England

explanation.surface: Counting how often a new set of nine detectives turned up in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'were in' applies only to the detectives, who sit inside the reshuffled nine; the church abbreviation simply follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Incidence is the rate at which something happens, as in the incidence of a disease.

clue.text: Runs second editions

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a print run or print is an edition of a book

explanation.surface: A publisher puts out second editions of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks like the print runs of the surface, but it is the definition: fast dashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprints are short fast races or dashes, so they are runs.

clue.text: Father turned up helping people to start sharing

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something up means reading it from bottom to top
the start of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
a helping of food is a portion
men as people in general
the opening letter of to

explanation.surface: Dad arrives to help people get started sharing things out.
explanation.definitionFit: Apportionment is the dividing up and sharing out of something among people.

clue.text: Objections to going back for the counterfoil

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: ifs and buts: buts are objections

explanation.surface: Raising objections to returning the counterfoil of a cheque or ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub is the part of a cheque or ticket kept as a record, the counterfoil.

clue.text: Make soundproof?

blocks.note: surface reading: insulate a room so noise cannot get through
setter's reading: make proof, a lasting record, of sound

explanation.walkthrough: Soundproof suggests insulation; split it into 'sound' and 'proof' and it means capturing audio as evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To capture audio on magnetic tape makes a permanent record of what was said.

clue.text: Horrified that some national flag has to be taken down

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a part of them is used, a run of letters inside

blocks.note: surface padding, setting the scene of a national flag
a run of letters across these words
surface padding: a flag being lowered, as at a time of mourning

explanation.surface: Shocked that a national flag must be lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest of the clue, 'national' and 'be taken down', just completes the picture of a flag being lowered.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with horror or shock, a synonym of horrified.

clue.text: Far from rare to see last ball of series

blocks.note: first meaning: cooked too long, the opposite of a rare steak
second meaning, read as two words: when the last ball of a series is bowled, the cricket over is done

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a series of six balls bowled from one end; after the last one, the over is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat cooked well past rare is overdone, and a completed over in cricket is an over done.

clue.text: Oscar, perhaps, would make an announcement about "Et tu …" anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in no particular order, so the letters are jumbled
about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to state is to declare or announce
the letters of et tu rearranged

explanation.surface: An Oscar winner's acceptance speech garbles Caesar's famous 'Et tu, Brute'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar, perhaps' defines by example, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oscar is a small statue given as an award, an example of a statuette.

clue.text: Gave evidence on how healthy group come up and die out

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading from bottom to top
out can mean wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: fit means in good health
a set is a group
the letters of die rearranged

explanation.surface: A witness gave evidence about how a fit group rose up and then perished.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to give evidence under oath in court.

clue.text: Sat around accepting it's no good to worry

indicators.note: around suggests letters turned about and shuffled into a new order
accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the letters of sat rearranged
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: Someone sat around admitting there was no point in worrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a feeling of deep anxiety or dread, a noun sense of worry.

clue.text: River in Kent? That's not right!

blocks.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
Kent is in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: Someone claims a river is in Kent and is told that is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the Fal is in Cornwall, not Kent, so the answer itself comments on the wordplay. Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something false is untrue or incorrect, the opposite of right.

clue.text: A new customer left out, being very old

indicators.note: something left out is omitted, so a letter must be dropped from the word

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
a client is a customer
L is the abbreviation for left, and it is this that goes

explanation.surface: A new customer was ignored for being elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' does double duty: left supplies L, and out says to remove it from the customer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means belonging to the distant past, so extremely old.

clue.text: On entering, executes the numskulls

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so this piece is placed within another

blocks.note: to behead is to execute by cutting off the head
taken as written

explanation.surface: On arrival, someone puts the idiots to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Boneheads and numskulls are both slang for stupid people, as if their heads were solid.

clue.text: Fire or part of one

blocks.note: first meaning: one of the four classical ...
second meaning: a component of a whole

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' is an example of the first sense, the ancient four of earth, air, fire and water.
explanation.definitionFit: An element is both a classical basic substance like fire and a constituent piece of a larger whole.

clue.text: Daughter can weaken

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
if someone can, they are able

explanation.surface: A daughter is able to sap someone's strength.
explanation.definitionFit: To disable is to put out of action or reduce capability, so to weaken.

clue.text: Catty issue

blocks.note: surface reading: a spiteful quarrel or bitchy matter
setter's reading: issue meaning offspring, so the offspring of a cat

explanation.walkthrough: Catty usually means spiteful and issue a topic; read literally, issue is offspring and catty means of a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A young cat is the offspring, or issue, of a cat.

clue.text: The fourth act is mayhem initially, involving militant behaviour

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: act IV, the fourth act of a play in Roman numerals
taken as written
the opening letter of mayhem

explanation.surface: In a play's fourth act everything turns chaotic with militant behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: Acts of a play are numbered in Roman numerals, so the fourth is act IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Activism is vigorous campaigning for a political or social cause.

clue.text: Pardon for former copper on fringes of swindle

indicators.note: the fringes of something are its edges, so only its outer letters are kept

blocks.note: ex means former
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the first and last letters of swindle

explanation.surface: A retired policeman seeks a pardon for being involved at the edges of a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer, but here it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To pardon a fault is to excuse it, forgiving the offender.

clue.text: Secret plot got a bishop in a state

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these go within another piece

blocks.note: Cal. is an abbreviation for California, a US state
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
taken as written

explanation.surface: A conspiracy has led to a bishop being installed somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop and the article go inside the abbreviation for California, with the bishop first.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabal is a small secret group of plotters, and by extension their intrigue.

clue.text: Opposition to mixed ancestries …

indicators.note: something mixed has its parts stirred together in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of ancestries rearranged

explanation.surface: Objection to people with mixed family origins, continued in the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistance is the act of opposing or refusing something, a synonym of opposition.

clue.text: … by holding a book, a little one

indicators.note: holding means gripping something inside, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: taken as written
a, plus B, the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue: opposition by someone clutching a book, a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby is an infant, a little one in everyday speech.

clue.text: One reads of French in exploit

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so this piece goes within another

blocks.note: a stunt is a daring feat or exploit
de is French for of

explanation.surface: Someone reads a French text about a daring exploit.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you 'read' a subject at university, so one who reads is a student.
explanation.definitionFit: A British undergraduate is said to read history or law, so a student is one who reads.

clue.text: A row outside the Spanish studio

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so this piece wraps around another

blocks.note: taken as written
a tier is a row, as of seats
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A tier of seating surrounds a Spanish art studio.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's workshop, borrowed from French.
